findings.scenario: Both counted fixtures accept from nonblocking listeners and read_request immediately expects blocking reads. On Darwin an accepted stream inherits the nonblocking mode, so a connection accepted before the client's first or complete write returns WouldBlock and panics before the intended protocol/consumer assertion. The macos-15 whole-Host validation path includes these tests.
findings.rationale: Root re-read both accept branches, the complete shared request reader, the R6 HTTP helper and the existing macOS whole-Host workflow step. This is a concrete retained-scope oracle defect; it is not an observed Actions failure or a production socket defect. The earlier R5 P3 decision only normalized the newly added HTTP helper; this finding identifies two additional original-scope callers and does not reverse that decision.
findings.change: Normalize TcpStream to blocking at the start of the existing read_request helper, before its five-second read timeout and first read. Remove the now-redundant HTTP helper-only normalization. Retain every required test, bounded reads, complete response/control data, request-count and one-wrapper assertions.
